{"assignee":"","description":"PROBLEM
compute_is_origin (crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs ~L277-291 at f4c6b688) answers 'does the CALLER have a ParticipantIdentity with this calendarAddress?' via backend.get_objects::<ParticipantIdentity>(caller, ...). Spec (draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33 §5) asks whether 'the account will receive messages sent to the organizerCalendarAddress URI'. Since -32 ParticipantIdentity is per user ('specific to the authenticated user as well as the account'), so on a multi-user backend isOrigin would depend on who created/edited the event. Neil Jenkins, jmap@ietf.org 2026-10-19 (thread 'draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-33: how does the server determine isOrigin?'): 'isOrigin should not depend on the user accessing the calendar; it should be the same for everyone.' Mark told the list 2026-11-01 crate-jmap will move to an account-level set. No current backend is multi-user (all 8 CalendarsBackend impls use CallerCtx = ()), so this is a latent bug: fix the contract now so multi-user backends can't get it wrong.

PLAN (approved design; 4 files)
1. crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs: add to trait CalendarsBackend:
     fn account_receives_at(&self, caller: &Self::CallerCtx, account_id: &Id, uri: &str) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send
   (match the async style of the neighbouring trait methods). Doc: account-level, server-defined answer to 'will this account receive messages sent to uri'; MUST NOT depend on which user is calling; cite §5 isOrigin. DEFAULT IMPL = today's behaviour: get_objects::<ParticipantIdentity>(caller, account_id, None, None) and exact string match on calendar_address. Mark it with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling: correct only when every caller sees all of the account's identities (single-user backends); multi-user backends must override.
2. crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs: compute_is_origin keeps its signature and the organizer==None => true branch, but calls backend.account_receives_at(caller, account_id, address) instead of get_objects. Keep the map_err to server_fail_value_from_backend. Do NOT change when it runs (create, copy, organizerCalendarAddress change only). Keep the existing ponytail comment about no recompute when identities change (still true) and drop the part that describes the identity scan, since that now lives in the default impl. Update the fn doc comment to say it delegates to account_receives_at.
3. crate-jmap-calendars-server/tests/common/mod.rs: the delegating test backend (FaultyBackend wrapping MemoryBackend) gets a field like extra_receives_at: Mutex<Vec<String>> plus a builder/setter, and overrides account_receives_at to return true if the uri is in that list, else delegate to inner.
4. crate-jmap-calendars-server/tests/event_origin_calendar_ids.rs: new regression test. Backend has acc1 with NO ParticipantIdentity seeded (caller sees none), but extra_receives_at = [OWN]. Create an event with organizerCalendarAddress OWN => isOrigin true. Oracle: the §5 isOrigin text already quoted at the top of that file. Must FAIL against the pre-fix code (it returns false there) - check that before landing. Also update that file's header comment 'The account's own addresses are its ParticipantIdentity calendarAddress values' to say they come from CalendarsBackend::account_receives_at (defaulting to the identity scan). Existing tests in that file must pass unchanged.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE
Required trait method with no default: forces every backend to decide, but all 8 current impls are single-user where the default is correct, so it would touch 7 mock impls (calendar.rs, lib.rs, event.rs x3, principal.rs, tests/common) for no behaviour change.

DONE WHEN
- Steps 1-4 landed; new test fails on old code, passes on new.
- cargo fmt --all; cargo clippy -p jmap-calendars-server --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test -p jmap-calendars-server all clean (use the crate's real package name).
- Note on close: the original done-condition ('two users with different identities get the same isOrigin') isn't directly testable without a multi-user test backend (none exists; ~300 lines to build). The step-4 test proves the same contract from the other side: the answer comes from the account-level method, not the caller's visible identities.","status":"open"}
